title: Earthquake response spectra
summary: How ground shaking excites buildings of different natural periods, why damping limits resonance, and how distance filters the shaking toward long periods.

concepts.label: Ground motion
concepts.description: Shaking recorded at a station: peak acceleration (PGA, %g), velocity (PGV, cm/s).

facts.text: ShakeMap station lists give peak values per channel for each recording station.

children.label: Spectral acceleration
children.description: SA(T): peak response of a 5%-damped oscillator of period T to the record, %g.

children.label: Dynamic amplification
children.description: SA(T)/PGA: how much an oscillator amplifies the ground motion.

concepts.label: Single-degree-of-freedom oscillator
concepts.description: A mass on a spring with a damper: the model behind the response spectrum.

facts.text: At resonance the steady-state amplification of a lightly damped oscillator is about 1/(2ζ).

children.label: Natural period
children.description: The period at which the structure oscillates freely; about N/10 s for an N-storey building.

children.label: Damping ratio
children.description: The fraction of critical damping; about 5% for ordinary buildings.

children.label: Multi-storey modes
children.description: Real buildings have higher modes and soil–structure interaction, not in this model.

concepts.label: Seismic attenuation
concepts.description: Loss of wave amplitude with distance: geometric spreading plus anelastic absorption (quality factor Q).

facts.text: Absorption per wavelength is fixed by Q, so higher frequencies lose more per kilometre.

children.label: Distance from rupture
children.description: ShakeMap's distance to the fault rupture, km.

children.label: Spectral shape ratio
children.description: SA(3 s)/SA(0.3 s): tall-building over low-building shaking.

children.label: Site amplification
children.description: Soft soils and sedimentary basins (low Vs30) amplify long periods.

concepts.label: Earthquake source
concepts.description: The M7.1 Ridgecrest mainshock, 6 July 2019; magnitude and rupture length set the corner period of the source spectrum.
